content.text:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the silhouetted figure at the observation-deck rail in <Picture 1>, seen from behind: dark hair gathered into a ponytail, a long black uniform coat with shoulder panels and a belt, standing with both hands resting on the rail, back to the camera and facing the viewport; the face is never visible.
<Subject 2> is the bridge observation-deck interior in <Picture 1>: a large rectangular viewport with a heavy metal frame and a rail along the sill, a reflective metal floor with strip highlights, and cold low-key lighting that silhouettes anyone standing at the glass.
<Subject 3> is the deep-space background seen through the viewport in <Picture 1>: a deep blue-black nebula band with dense star points whose self-luminous glow backlights the deck.
<Subject 4> is the trailer title package in <Picture 1>: two lines of wide-letter-spaced uppercase sans-serif text, "THE LAST FLEET LEFT EARTH" above "SHE WAS NOT ON BOARD", set in cool gray-white rather than pure white, with restrained inner glow, a faint edge halo and a subtle material texture; the wording, spelling and line order stay unchanged.
<Subject 5> is the fleet in <Picture 1>: several dark-hulled science-fiction warships with faint window lights, two larger capital ships balanced to the left and right of the formation and smaller craft scattered between them across the nebula.
<Picture 1> is the composition anchor for the title-reveal moment of [Shot 1]: it defines the centered figure inside the nested viewport frame, the balanced fleet placement on both sides, and the title band across the upper middle. It does not lock the 0.00-second frame.

summary:
[reference generation] The target video is a 15-second cinematic trailer beat built from <Picture 1>: <Subject 1> stands at the rail of <Subject 2> while <Subject 5> spreads across <Subject 3> behind the glass and <Subject 4> emerges from the deep-space dark and settles over the composition; the fleet's jump floods the viewport with light, the deck shudders, a hard flash and a short black gap cover the departure, and the title returns over the emptied star field with the lone figure still at the rail.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2], the lower-left edge of [Shot 3], and [Shot 4]): fully_preserved - the ponytail, black uniform coat, back-facing orientation and hands-on-rail position carry through every appearance; the shudder and the bracing are added motion rather than a change of appearance.
<Subject 2> (all shots): fully_preserved - the viewport, frame, sill rail, reflective floor and cold low-key lighting are unchanged; the shaking is motion, not a change of structure.
<Subject 3> (all shots): fully_preserved - the nebula band, star density and backlight remain; only the residual jump streaks fade through them in [Shot 4].
<Subject 4> ([Shot 1], [Shot 4]): fully_preserved - wording, wide letter spacing, cool non-white tone, restrained glow, edge halo and material texture are kept; the requested animation adds the reveal, the starlight sweep, the spacing expansion, the afterimage and the black flash without altering the lettering.
<Subject 5> ([Shot 1], [Shot 2], [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - the formation, dark hulls and faint window lights are kept while the fleet is on screen; it leaves the sky at the jump, which is the required action rather than a loss of reference fidelity.
<Picture 1> ([Shot 1] composition anchor): fully_preserved - the framing, centered figure, balanced fleet placement and title band are reproduced at the title-reveal moment; the video then continues past that frame.

detailed_description:
The target video is a cinematic live-action science-fiction trailer segment in a 16:9 anamorphic frame, cool and desaturated with deep-space blacks, restrained bloom, faint lens flare and fine film grain, matching the palette and lighting of <Picture 1>. Cutting is fast and hard, and the short black beat is used only where the action creates it.
[Shot 1] The shot opens in near-darkness inside the observation deck of <Subject 2>, with the darkest region of <Subject 3> centered in the viewport. <Subject 4> emerges from that dark: the cool gray-white letterforms are at first barely separable from the nebula shadow, then a band of starlight sweeps across the lettering from left to right and lights its edges as the letter spacing widens to its final value, a faint afterimage trailing each letter while the restrained glow and thin edge halo hold; both lines stay fully inside the frame with clear margins. <Subject 1> stands centered at the rail with both hands on it, back to the camera, silhouetted against the nebula, and <Subject 5> spreads across the star field on both sides behind the glass. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed until the framing matches the composition of <Picture 1>. Near the end of the shot, points of drive light gather along the fleet's hulls and swell, the glass brightens, and the deck begins a fine low tremble that shivers the edge of the figure's coat; the low deck hum deepens with the growing light and small metal ticks come from the structures.
[Shot 2] At 00:04.000, the shot cuts to a closer view of <Subject 1> from behind and slightly to the side, with the viewport and <Subject 5> beyond it. The shudder deepens and the frame trembles with it; the figure's hands tighten around the rail and her shoulders rise as her ponytail and coat hem shake. Beyond the glass the fleet's hulls begin to stretch, the light at the formation core swells, and the glass floods until her silhouette thins to a bright outline. A rising low rumble and metallic groans build with the growing light, and a short tense breath is audible under them.
[Shot 3] At 00:07.200, the shot cuts to a tighter view of the viewport glass filling the frame, with the dark edge of the figure's shoulder at the lower left. The two capital ships pull apart into bright streaks as the formation compresses and stretches away, and the gathered light at the core discharges through the glass in a hard flash that whites out the whole frame with no interior detail left legible; the picture then drops into a brief black gap. A hard crack and a low impact land on the flash and cut the rumble off, and near-silence holds through the black beat.
[Shot 4] At 00:09.200, the shot opens out of the black gap on the deck: the viewport holds only <Subject 3>, with no ships, and a few residual luminous streaks fade into the star field as the shudder dies away. <Subject 1> is still in the same place with her hands on the rail, ponytail and coat settling. <Subject 4> returns as a cool afterimage that sharpens into the settled lettering at its final spacing, its restrained glow and thin edge halo steady; the camera pushes in slowly with small amplitude toward the lettering as the glow dims to a faint trace over the emptied star field, the figure small and still at the rail below. A long low tone fades with the residual streaks, a few metal ticks follow the settling structures, and the low deck hum continues under the ending.

overall_soundscape:
A low deck hum runs through the whole video, with faint metal ticking and occasional structural groans inside the enclosed bridge observation deck. The shudder of the deck is audible as a fine metallic rattle on the rail and floor, and the room tone stays cold and close, with no exterior space noise beyond the glass.

non_diegetic_music:
A sustained low synth drone at a slow tempo carries the opening, thickening as the light gathers, with a single hard percussive hit at the flash and a drop to near-silence through the black gap, then a quiet sustained low string pad that fades out with the title's glow.
